requirement.original: Make image fetch failure block the generate-and-deploy pipeline instead of silently continuing
requirement.clarified: Image fetch failures in Step 1 of generate-and-deploy.sh are silently swallowed by `|| echo` constructs. Add one retry on failure; if the retry also fails, emit a loud (RED/banner) warning and continue -- images are optional but degradation must be visible in the log.
requirement.what: Replace all three `|| echo` failure handlers on fetch-images-batch.py call sites with a retry-once-then-warn-loudly pattern implemented as a reusable bash function
requirement.why: Broken image fetches silently deploy without images; operators have no signal that the output is degraded until they manually inspect the live page

included: Retry logic (one retry = two total attempts) for all three fetch-images-batch.py call sites
Loud RED warning with exit code on double failure
Pipeline continues after warning (images remain optional)
Single helper function to avoid copy-paste across call sites

success_criteria: fetch-images-batch.py is called a second time when the first attempt exits non-zero
A RED multi-line warning containing FAILED or WARNING is printed when both attempts fail
Steps 2-5 complete successfully even after a double image-fetch failure
No behavioral change when fetch-images-batch.py exits zero on first attempt
All three call sites (lines 93, 101, 104) apply the same logic
constraints: set -euo pipefail is active; exit code must be captured explicitly, not left to propagate
2>/dev/null on Python invocations should be preserved on first attempt; stderr may surface on retry failure for diagnostics
All three call sites pass different argument combinations; helper function must forward arguments faithfully

root_cause_analysis.symptom: Image fetch failures produce no visible signal in the deploy log; the pipeline completes and deploys with broken or missing images without any warning
root_cause_analysis.root_cause: All three call sites of fetch-images-batch.py in Step 1 use `|| echo` or `|| echo -e` to absorb non-zero exit codes, converting hard failures into informational-looking single-line messages that blend into normal log output. There is no retry and no visual distinction between a successful fetch and a failed one.
root_cause_analysis.root_cause_commit: N/A - pattern present from initial script authorship; not introduced by a specific recent commit
root_cause_analysis.why_introduced: The `|| echo` pattern was used to intentionally bypass `set -euo pipefail` so images could remain optional and not abort the pipeline
root_cause_analysis.why_problematic: Bypassing the error entirely makes failures invisible. An operator reading the log cannot distinguish 'fetch succeeded' from 'fetch failed silently'. Broken deployments go undetected.
root_cause_analysis.timeline: Present since at least commit 74d3527 (2026-02-13); no change to failure handling in subsequent commits

development_approach.strategy: Define a bash helper function `fetch_images_with_retry` before the Step 1 block. The function accepts all arguments, runs fetch-images-batch.py once, checks the exit code, retries once on failure (optionally with a 1-2s sleep), and on second failure prints a RED multi-line banner before returning 0 (so the pipeline continues). Replace all three `|| echo` patterns with calls to this function.
development_approach.validation_approach: Run the pipeline with a deliberately broken plan ID or by temporarily making fetch-images-batch.py exit non-zero; verify (1) two invocation attempts appear in the log, (2) a RED warning banner is printed, (3) HTML generation (Step 2) still runs. Also run against a valid plan to confirm silent success path is unchanged.

research_findings.reason: Straightforward bash error handling pattern with clear root cause. No architectural decision or new integration involved.
